title: Seasonal H-alpha slopes remove at most 12.6 percent of 66.83-day signal information in 250 GJ 581 HARPS visits
abstract: We measure how much a linear H-alpha correction can remove from a coherent 66.83-day sine wave in 250 GJ 581 HARPS-RVBank version 02 visits. After a fixed baseline fit, seven seasonal slopes remove 3.42 to 12.53 percent of signal information over all phases. One shared slope removes at most 5.74 percent. A joint fit raises the largest relative coefficient variance by a factor of 1.143. Across 32 weight and season-boundary cases, the largest seasonal loss is 9.82 to 14.42 percent. Exact projections, noiseless injections, and covariance checks agree. These results assume measured H-alpha values and diagonal velocity noise. They do not establish a planet or an activity cause. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes, and external-data retrieval steps are included. Raw data and record-level derivatives are excluded.

display.caption: The shaded band gives the exact range over signal phase under the stated baseline and diagonal noise model. The two panels use one shared slope or seven seasonal slopes. The dotted line marks 66.83 days.
